frases.texto: It had not rained for such a long time that the ground was cracked like a broken biscuit, and the wheat in the fields had withered.
frases.fala: It had not rained for such a long time that the ground was cracked like a broken biscuit, and the wheat in the fields had withered.

frases.texto: Suddenly, far off down the road, there appeared a PILGRIMAGE: a long line of country folk walking slowly and singing to the rhythm of a TAMBOURINE.
frases.fala: Suddenly, far off down the road, there appeared a pilgrimage: a long line of country folk walking slowly and singing to the rhythm of a tambourine.

frases.texto: At the front, four men carried a litter on their shoulders, a kind of wooden platform decorated with flowers.
frases.fala: At the front, four men carried a litter on their shoulders, a kind of wooden platform decorated with flowers.

frases.texto: And atop the litter sat a figure covered all over in a blue MANTLE.
frases.fala: And atop the litter sat a figure covered all over in a blue mantle.

frases.texto: Don Quixote narrowed his eyes and nearly tumbled from his saddle: “A lady wrapped in a mantle, carried by a band of strangers!
frases.fala: Don Quixote narrowed his eyes and nearly tumbled from his saddle: A lady wrapped in a mantle, carried by a band of strangers!

frases.texto: Those villains are whisking a princess away!”
frases.fala: Those villains are whisking a princess away!

frases.texto: Sancho scratched his head: “A princess?
frases.fala: Sancho scratched his head: A princess?

frases.texto: Master, that looks like a procession to me...”
frases.fala: Master, that looks like a procession to me...

frases.texto: But Don Quixote wasn’t listening any more.
frases.fala: But Don Quixote wasn’t listening any more.

frases.texto: He adjusted his basin-helmet, pointed his lance and cried: “Onwards, Rocinante!
frases.fala: He adjusted his basin-helmet, pointed his lance and cried: Onwards, Rocinante!

frases.texto: Let us rescue the lady!”
frases.fala: Let us rescue the lady!

frases.texto: Rocinante, who had been dozing on his feet, got such a fright that he set off in a clumsy gallop, kicking up dust in all directions.
frases.fala: Rocinante, who had been dozing on his feet, got such a fright that he set off in a clumsy gallop, kicking up dust in all directions.

frases.texto: The priest dropped his hat, Master Nicolás choked on his sip of water, and Sancho hopped off his donkey and dashed after his master, his short little legs flying: “There he goes again!”
frases.fala: The priest dropped his hat, Master Nicolás choked on his sip of water, and Sancho hopped off his donkey and dashed after his master, his short little legs flying: There he goes again!

frases.texto: Chapter 31. Neighbours on the Road. A Saint, Not a Princess
frases.fala: Chapter 31. Neighbours on the Road. A Saint, Not a Princess

frases.texto: Sancho ran as he had never run before in all his life.
frases.fala: Sancho ran as he had never run before in all his life.

frases.texto: He sprinted in front of Rocinante, threw his arms wide and squeezed his eyes shut: “Stop, master!
frases.fala: He sprinted in front of Rocinante, threw his arms wide and squeezed his eyes shut: Stop, master!

frases.texto: Stop, for the love of goodness!”
frases.fala: Stop, for the love of goodness!

frases.texto: Rocinante stopped so suddenly that Don Quixote slid forwards and wound up hugging the horse’s neck, with the basin-helmet slipping down over his eyes.
frases.fala: Rocinante stopped so suddenly that Don Quixote slid forwards and wound up hugging the horse’s neck, with the basin-helmet slipping down over his eyes.

frases.texto: And Sancho, with his eyes still tightly shut, kept asking: “Has he stopped yet?
frases.fala: And Sancho, with his eyes still tightly shut, kept asking: Has he stopped yet?

frases.texto: Can I open my eyes?”
frases.fala: Can I open my eyes?

frases.texto: “It isn’t a princess at all, my lord!” he explained, puffing and panting.
frases.fala: It isn’t a princess at all, my lord! he explained, puffing and panting.

frases.texto: “It’s a statue of a SAINT!
frases.fala: It’s a statue of a saint!

frases.texto: And these people aren’t bandits: they’re the FARMERS from our own lands, our neighbours!
frases.fala: And these people aren’t bandits: they’re the farmers from our own lands, our neighbours!

frases.texto: They’re praying for rain to fall and for the wheat to grow!”
frases.fala: They’re praying for rain to fall and for the wheat to grow!

frases.texto: Don Quixote straightened his basin-helmet and took a good look.
frases.fala: Don Quixote straightened his basin-helmet and took a good look.

frases.texto: Up close, he could see everything: the calm face of the saint beneath her blue mantle, the flowers on the litter, the weathered hands of the farmers and their sun-browned faces.
frases.fala: Up close, he could see everything: the calm face of the saint beneath her blue mantle, the flowers on the litter, the weathered hands of the farmers and their sun-browned faces.

frases.texto: Then he climbed down from his horse, took off his basin-helmet and bowed his head: “Forgive my mistake, good people.
frases.fala: Then he climbed down from his horse, took off his basin-helmet and bowed his head: Forgive my mistake, good people.

frases.texto: I came to rescue a lady... and I found people who tend the land with patience and hope.
frases.fala: I came to rescue a lady... and I found people who tend the land with patience and hope.

frases.texto: There is no greater courage than that.”
frases.fala: There is no greater courage than that.

frases.texto: An elderly man from the pilgrimage smiled warmly: “Well, if it isn’t Master Alonso from our village!
frases.fala: An elderly man from the pilgrimage smiled warmly: Well, if it isn’t Master Alonso from our village!

frases.texto: You are almost home!”
frases.fala: You are almost home!

frases.texto: And he offered him a cup of fresh cool water and a bunch of wild FLOWERS.
frases.fala: And he offered him a cup of fresh cool water and a bunch of wild flowers.

frases.texto: Don Quixote drank gratefully, and the pilgrimage went singing on down the road, with Sancho clapping along to the beat of the tambourine.
frases.fala: Don Quixote drank gratefully, and the pilgrimage went singing on down the road, with Sancho clapping along to the beat of the tambourine.

frases.texto: Chapter 32. Back Home. A Big Hug for the Donkey
frases.fala: Chapter 32. Back Home. A Big Hug for the Donkey

frases.texto: It was lunchtime on Sunday when the ox cart rolled slowly into the VILLAGE, with Don Quixote riding on Rocinante right alongside.
frases.fala: It was lunchtime on Sunday when the ox cart rolled slowly into the village, with Don Quixote riding on Rocinante right alongside.

frases.texto: The church bells rang out, and the neighbours hurried to their windows: “Look who has arrived!
frases.fala: The church bells rang out, and the neighbours hurried to their windows: Look who has arrived!

frases.texto: It’s Master Alonso!”
frases.fala: It’s Master Alonso!

frases.texto: From the gentleman’s house came his niece Antonia and the housekeeper, running out into the street.
frases.fala: From the gentleman’s house came his niece Antonia and the housekeeper, running out into the street.

frases.texto: The two of them hugged Don Quixote, crying and laughing at the same time: “Our dear uncle has come back!
frases.fala: The two of them hugged Don Quixote, crying and laughing at the same time: Our dear uncle has come back!

frases.texto: How we missed you!”
frases.fala: How we missed you!

frases.texto: Across the street came Teresa Panza, Sancho’s WIFE, holding their little daughter Sanchica by the hand.
frases.fala: Across the street came Teresa Panza, Sancho’s wife, holding their little daughter Sanchica by the hand.

frases.texto: Sancho hopped off his donkey and spread his arms, beaming with joy... but the two of them hurried straight past him and threw their arms around the donkey!
frases.fala: Sancho hopped off his donkey and spread his arms, beaming with joy... but the two of them hurried straight past him and threw their arms around the donkey!

frases.texto: “How lovely to have you back, little donkey!” said Teresa.
frases.fala: How lovely to have you back, little donkey! said Teresa.

frases.texto: “You’re even plumper than before!”
frases.fala: You’re even plumper than before!

frases.texto: And Sancho stood there, with his arms open to the breeze: “What about me?
frases.fala: And Sancho stood there, with his arms open to the breeze: What about me?

frases.texto: Doesn’t anyone hug the squire?”
frases.fala: Doesn’t anyone hug the squire?

frases.texto: Teresa laughed and at last gave her husband a great big squeeze.
frases.fala: Teresa laughed and at last gave her husband a great big squeeze.

frases.texto: But soon she wanted to know: “And the dresses you promised, my dear?
frases.fala: But soon she wanted to know: And the dresses you promised, my dear?

frases.texto: And that ISLAND you were going to rule?
frases.fala: And that island you were going to rule?

frases.texto: Did you bring it in your pocket?”
frases.fala: Did you bring it in your pocket?

frases.texto: “An island doesn’t fit in a pocket, my dear Teresa!” laughed Sancho.
frases.fala: An island doesn’t fit in a pocket, my dear Teresa! laughed Sancho.

frases.texto: “But its time will come, you shall see!”
frases.fala: But its time will come, you shall see!

frases.texto: Dresses, he had none.
frases.fala: Dresses, he had none.

frases.texto: But he opened his saddlebag and took out some gold coins: they were the coins from the suitcase lost on the mountain, which his master had given him as a gift.
frases.fala: But he opened his saddlebag and took out some gold coins: they were the coins from the suitcase lost on the mountain, which his master had given him as a gift.

frases.texto: “These are for Sanchica’s new shoes!”

frases.texto: Then he pulled out the wooden spinning top, and the little girl gave a squeal of delight.
frases.fala: Then he pulled out the wooden spinning top, and the little girl gave a squeal of delight.

frases.texto: Then Sancho puffed out his chest: “And mark my words, my dears: one day you will see me as the GOVERNOR of my very own island!”

frases.texto: Chapter 33. Dreams at the Window. The Knight’s Rest
frases.fala: Chapter 33. Dreams at the Window. The Knight’s Rest

frases.texto: Night fell softly over La Mancha and covered the little white houses of the village with a sky full of STARS.
frases.fala: Night fell softly over La Mancha and covered the little white houses of the village with a sky full of stars.

frases.texto: In his cosy, tidy bedroom, his niece and the housekeeper gently took off Don Quixote’s battered armour, bathed his scratches with flower water and dressed him in a soft nightshirt.
frases.fala: In his cosy, tidy bedroom, his niece and the housekeeper gently took off Don Quixote’s battered armour, bathed his scratches with flower water and dressed him in a soft nightshirt.

frases.texto: He had kept his word of honour: he was home.
frases.fala: He had kept his word of honour: he was home.

frases.texto: Tucked into his soft bed, smelling of lavender, he sipped a bowl of hot broth.
frases.fala: Tucked into his soft bed, smelling of lavender, he sipped a bowl of hot broth.

frases.texto: Out in the stable, Rocinante munched his hay, as happy as can be.
frases.fala: Out in the stable, Rocinante munched his hay, as happy as can be.

frases.texto: Meanwhile, the adventures of the knight with the basin on his head were passing from mouth to mouth.
frases.fala: Meanwhile, the adventures of the knight with the basin on his head were passing from mouth to mouth.

frases.texto: Goatherds told travellers, travellers told muleteers, and the muleteers carried the stories along the roads, all the way to great and distant cities.
